question.problem:
A scientist experiments with bacteria. The number of bacteria $B(t)$ in his experiment increases at a rate proportional to the number of bacteria at that moment. Additionally, due to environmental conditions, $250$ bacteria die every hour.
What is the differential equation that describes the rate of change in the population of bacteria at time $t,$ where $t$ is the time in hours?

current_example.problem: Since the year $2000$, a herd of antelopes multiplies at a rate proportional to their population. Also, the number of antelopes in the herd decreases by $20$ antelopes per year due to predators. What differential equation describes the rate of change in the population of antelopes at time $t,$ where $t$ is the time (in years) since the year $2000?$
current_example.worked_solution:
The rate of change in the number of antelopes per year increases in proportion to $P$ and decreases by $20.$ The differential equation that describes this is

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}P}{\textrm{d}t}=kP - 20,
$$

where $k$ is a (positive) constant of proportionality.
